raw: {"analysis":"Both responses provide thorough, well-structured plans that cover all the stated constraints: manual build, manifest version check, privacy link validation, no experimental flags, hardware token signing via acting manager, flaky macOS accessibility check, and Director of Product approval. SXZ explicitly includes a deadline management section (target submission date relative to the compliance deadline) and human decision points for accessibility failure and token unavailability, which directly address the requester's urgency and known risks. BHK is also comprehensive but lacks an explicit deadline plan and frames the accessibility handling as 'bypassing' the auto-check rather than conditionally verifying on failure. SXZ also adds a binary-source hash integrity check and a rollback mitigation strategy, making it slightly more actionable and complete for the irreversible submission scenario.","verdict":"SXZ"}
